rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so this experiment tests a multimodal, multiprofile setup with PCA and ViT encoders, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion. It isolates the impact of advanced image encoding (ViT) and fusion strategy (weighted) while keeping RNA encoding simple (PCA). This balances exploration of key components (representation, fusion) and provides a baseline for comparing complexity vs performance.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile models with pca_n2000 and imagenet_vit_l perform well. This experiment tests whether switching to resnet50 image encoder and concat fusion (vs. weighted fusion and vit_l) improves performance, isolating the impact of image encoder and fusion method. It balances exploration of key design choices while staying within the multimodal multiprofile framework.

Existing evidence shows that config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, avgpool, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.635). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder with scvi_n200 while keeping other parameters identical, isolating the impact of RNA representation. This clarifies whether the RNA encoder choice significantly affects performance, a critical design decision with sparse evidence yet.

Existing evidence shows config_021 (scvi_n200 RNA, resnet50 image, avgpool, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether changing aggregation from avgpool to transformer (while keeping RNA/image encoders and fusion method constant) improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation. This balances exploitation of the current strong configuration with exploration of a critical design choice.

Existing evidence shows that scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder combinations achieve high accuracy (0.713 in config_013). This experiment tests whether replacing transformer aggregation (used in config_013) with avgpool aggregation affects performance, isolating the impact of aggregation method. It balances exploitation (building on successful RNA/image encoder pairs) and exploration (testing aggregation choices), providing critical insight into whether transformer aggregation is essential for high performance.

Existing evidence shows that using transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_013) achieves high accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests whether switching to concat fusion (while keeping transformer aggregation) impacts performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It directly compares two key design choices (fusion method) in a high-performing context, balancing exploitation of promising directions with exploration of critical parameters.

The existing evidence shows that config_013 (transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether changing the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 to scgpt while keeping other parameters (image encoder, aggregation, fusion) the same isolates the effect of the RNA representation. This is the best use of the next experiment as it directly evaluates a critical design choice (RNA encoder) with minimal parameter changes, avoiding unnecessary complexity.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_013) yield high accuracy. This experiment tests whether using pca_n2000 RNA encoder (vs scvi_n200) with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion maintains performance, isolating the impact of RNA representation. It avoids changing multiple variables and builds on the strong foundation of config_013.

Existing evidence shows that config_013 (scvi_n200, resnet50, transformer, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy. This experiment tests whether using the same RNA encoder (scvi_n200) with a different image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) and fusion method (concat) affects performance, isolating the impact of image encoder and fusion choices. It balances exploitation (using a proven RNA encoder) with exploration of critical design decisions.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation and concat fusion (as in config_009) yield high accuracy (0.7207). This experiment tests whether using pca_n2000 RNA encoder (vs scvi_n200 in config_009) affects performance with the same aggregation/fusion setup. It isolates the RNA encoder's impact while maintaining the promising combination of transformer aggregation and concat fusion, balancing exploitation of top-performing components with exploration of encoder variations.
